sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dc: <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/>
PREFIX event: <http://purl.org/NET/c4dm/event.owl#>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
PREFIX tl: <http://purl.org/NET/c4dm/timeline.owl#>
SELECT ?releaseEvent 
 WHERE {
 ?releaseEvent rdf:type mo:ReleaseEvent .
 ?releaseEvent dc:title "%s" .
 ?releaseEvent event:time ?date .
 ?date rdf:type tl:Instant .
 ?date tl:at "%s" .
 }
gold_question: Which release event with the given title occurred at the specified time?

review.note: The wording is fine but the concept of ReleaseEvent is not very NL friendly. It is probably used here to find the label that released the album. But on its own, this query does not make much sense to anyone not intimately familiar witht he ontology

model_output.nl_question: Which release event with the given title occurred at the specified time?
model_output.confidence_rationale: No directly relevant natural-language evidence matches this query, so the question is generated from the SPARQL. The query clearly filters for a ReleaseEvent by its title and exact time, which the wording reflects.

sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dc: <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
SELECT ?medium 
 WHERE {
 ?medium rdf:type mo:Record .
 ?medium dc:title "%s" .
 ?medium mo:record_number "%i" .
 }
gold_question: Which records have the given title and record number?

review.note: This one is looking for a specific disk within a larger release (usually a large compilation), by the disk title and number. The model would not be able to know it without knowing more about the ontology. The generated NL is not wrong, it just misses the context

model_output.nl_question: Which records have the given title and record number?
model_output.confidence_rationale: No provided CQ evidence matches this intent. The SPARQL clearly selects mo:Record entities filtered by a specified dc:title and mo:record_number, so the generated question reflects the query structure, but lacks supporting text evidence.

sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dtl: <http://www.DTL.org/schema/properties/>
PREFIX event: <http://purl.org/NET/c4dm/event.owl#>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
SELECT DISTINCT ?artist 
 WHERE {
 ?artist rdf:type mo:MusicArtist .
 ?artist foaf:name "%s" .
 ?performer dtl:musician ?artist .
 ?performance mo:performer ?performer .
 ?session event:sub_event ?performance .
 ?session mo:performer <%s> .
 }
gold_question: Find the musician by name who played in a session with the given performer

review.note: This seems to be a disambiguation query rather then search, since we already have the name. I would dismiss it

model_output.nl_question: Did the musician with the given name perform in the same session as the given performer?
model_output.confidence_rationale: No evidence snippet directly matches this co-performance/session intent, so the question is generated from the SPARQL. The SPARQL constrains an artist by name and checks for a performance within a session that also lists the given performer, which aligns with asking whether the named musician performed in the same session as the given performer.

PREFIX core: <https://w3id.org/arco/ontology/core/>
